author: WPB7
summary: The manuscript's curated source audit at CNA 7a64362e (pre-alpha.1), with alpha.1 and d6e9ff05 pointers: headline structural findings F-001..F-038, the subsystem matrix, a contradiction log of CNA's own documentation (C-001..C-019) and ten undocumented defects. The chapter packages already put nearly all of its current substance on the site, corrected to 009d40f5; many pin-era facts are now false (SpriteBatch truncation, by-value state, Game not registering XNB readers, zero concepts). Re-checked at TARGET, three CNA documentation defects survive (C-010, C-011, C-018) and are recorded as issue candidates; the renderer-versus-backend vocabulary and the name rule were added to the glossary.

concepts.text: The current campaign's product string 0.1.0-alpha.1 is distinct from the documentation source pin; nothing renames a development snapshot as a release.

concepts.text: Alpha.1 canonical facts: 50 identities over 46 families, singular mode plus opt-in multi-renderer sets, four platform selectors, three audio selectors, bounded compiled effects, ABI 0.7.0, 568 test sources, 8,263 definitions and 21 workflows.
concepts.note: The releases page keeps these as alpha.1 history beside the 009d40f5 values.

concepts.text: The source audit graded findings as VERIFIED, STRONG, PROBABLE or UNCERTAIN depending on whether implementation, tests and execution corroborated them.
concepts.note: The site uses a finer, coordinate-based vocabulary (source-verified, build-verified, runtime-observed, renderer-engaged, oracle-compared ...).

concepts.text: The audit pinned CNA develop at 7a64362e (2026-08-11, 'integration: reconcile parallel feature lanes') with a clean, read-only checkout.
concepts.note: Pin of a pre-alpha.1 edition: a record of how the book was made, with no CNA behaviour to document.

concepts.text: History at the pin showed a ten-lane integration series and an earlier 21-lane campaign that added renderer identities.
concepts.note: Integration history; most of the lanes concerned renderer families retired since.

concepts.text: Naming normalisation renamed graphics 'backend' vocabulary to 'renderer', normalised identities (OPENGLES became OPENGLES3, D3D spellings became DIRECTX*), renamed the NOXNA macro to CNAEXT and the free-direct-backed renderer from its old DX3 spelling to FREEDIRECT; old spellings are not aliases.
The tree moved from central src/ and include/ to modules/<name>/{src,include,tests,CMakeLists.txt} with enforced ownership and include isolation, and examples moved into their owning modules.
tokens: One public include root per module

concepts.text: At the audited pin CNA had 46 public renderer identities over 42 implementation families; always print both numbers, labelled, because several conflicting counts coexisted in the tree.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the registry is 25 identities over 21 families; the identity/family distinction is on the glossary.

concepts.text: The renderer identity registry is mechanically pinned: scripts/check_renderer_identities.py compares the registries and runs as the CTest RendererIdentityRegistry, which is what makes the published count trustworthy.
Build commands using CNA_GRAPHICS_BACKEND or an old identity spelling fail at configure with FATAL_ERROR 'CNA: Unknown graphics renderer'; there are no compatibility aliases.
CNA had no install, export or packaging step; it is consumed only by add_subdirectory plus target_link_libraries.

target.evidence: root CMakeLists.txt and modules/c-api/CMakeLists.txt (install/EXPORT CNACTargets, CNAConfig.cmake) at 009d40f5

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 the C++ framework still has no install/export rules, but the experimental C API has its own CNACApi install component and CMake package; the site states both.

concepts.text: CNA is a translation target, not a compatibility layer: it cannot run a C# assembly, porting means translating C# to C++, properties become getXProperty()/setXProperty(), and type and member names match XNA verbatim.

target.evidence: docs/migration-guide.md and public headers at 009d40f5; cna-and-xna page (checked)

concepts.text: 'Renderer' and 'backend' are different live concepts: a renderer is a graphics implementation, while 'backend' names service implementations in devices, input and networking (for example the compass, motion and vibration backends and ENetBackend).
concepts.note: Added to the glossary; corrected: at 009d40f5 two core graphics descriptor enums (GraphicsBackendCategory, GraphicsBackendMaturity) still use the word, so the split is not clean.

concepts.text: The free-direct-backed renderer was renamed so that its old identity could name a separate renderer on the real legacy DirectX API; the two were to be documented as separate renderers.
concepts.note: The separate legacy-DirectX renderer family is retired at 009d40f5; only FREEDIRECT remains (cmake/RendererIdentities.cmake).

concepts.text: C++23 is a toolchain floor, not a feature dependency: no std::expected, std::print, import std or coroutines; the code is written in a C++17/20 idiom.
tokens: Concepts are confined to a handful of public headers

target.evidence: text search of modules/, tests/ and tools/ at 009d40f5 (no std::expected/print/mdspan/flat_map/generator/coroutines; concepts in Texture3D.hpp, TextureCube.hpp, GltfMaterialBridge.hpp and content-pipeline headers)

concepts.note: The manuscript's 'zero C++20 concepts' is false at 009d40f5: concepts and requires-clauses appear in a handful of public headers; the site states this.

concepts.text: CNA's code uses separate namespace roots: Microsoft::Xna::Framework (XNA surface), Microsoft::Devices (Windows Phone sensors), CNA:: (own layer), System:: and SharpRuntime:: (sharp-runtime); the name CNA is never expanded.
concepts.note: Corrected: Microsoft::Xna::Framework::Design and ::Content::Pipeline, absent at the audited pin, exist at 009d40f5 (design and content-pipeline modules). The name rule was added to the glossary (wpb7-name-cna).

concepts.text: CNA consumes sharp-runtime through System/... include paths mirroring .NET type names; the SharpRuntime/-prefixed headers are only the library's own alias surface, not the extent of the dependency.

target.evidence: CNA includes of System/ and SharpRuntime/ headers at 009d40f5; components-and-consumption (checked)

concepts.note: The manuscript's count (54 headers at its pin) is not carried over.

concepts.text: The exception convention splits by layer: the XNA-facing surface throws .NET-shaped System:: exceptions such as ObjectDisposedException, while renderers throw std::runtime_error for 'this renderer cannot do that', matching IGraphicsRenderer's throwing defaults.

target.evidence: modules/graphics/src/Xna and modules/renderers at 009d40f5; IGraphicsRenderer.hpp defaults

concepts.text: The project's canonical term is renderer: GraphicsRendererType, CNA_GRAPHICS_RENDERER, cmake/RendererSelection.cmake and modules/renderers.
ASCII output is not a renderer: it is AsciiPostProcessEffect in graphics-ext, a renderer-neutral glyph-grid post-process that applies to any renderer's output.
NOXNA was renamed CNAEXT; the CNAEXT marker (an empty macro on non-XNA declarations) and the CNA_CNAEXT option (the optional graphics-ext layer) are different things.
tokens: It is not the CNA_CNAEXT option

concepts.text: Root build options include CNA_USE_CCACHE (ON), CNA_BUILD_TESTS (ON), CNA_BUILD_EXAMPLES (ON), CNA_CNAEXT (OFF), CNA_DEVICES (OFF) and CNA_ENABLE_NET (ON).
The module layout is physical and enforced, 15 modules wide at the pin, with renderers dominating the file count.
tokens: One public include root per module
concepts.note: More modules exist at 009d40f5 (content-pipeline, design, diagnostics, inspector, phone, platform, video-ffmpeg ...); the per-module file counts are not carried over.

concepts.text: The book at audit start had 575 pages, 9 parts, 49 chapters and 6 appendices; its largest chapters were the backend architecture, content and math chapters.
concepts.note: Manuscript metrics: a record of how the book was made, with no CNA behaviour to document.

concepts.text: All ten Phase A research areas (architecture/build, 3D/glTF/CNJ, content/XNB/CNJ, renderer catalogue, graphics core/effects, services, testing, platforms, siblings, framework core/math) were delivered as raw reports.
concepts.note: Book research process; each report is recorded as its own aux unit.

concepts.text: The renderer count was settled by three independent derivations (CMake STRINGS tokens, the enum, and the check script) at 46 identities over 42 families.
concepts.note: The single registry file is the source at 009d40f5 (25 identities over 21 families).

concepts.text: The content module is four subsystems under one facade: the XNB reader stack, the CNJ JSON format and loose-file readers, the shared glTF import core, and ContentManager.
.xnb reading is real: canonical readers are registered, LZX is a port of FNA's decoder compared against FNA, and real externally produced .xnb fixtures are committed.
concepts.note: At 009d40f5 there are 61 built-in readers (60 without native int128) and the ladder is .xnb, .cnb, .cnj, native; the pin's 50 readers and order are not carried over.

concepts.text: Game never registers the built-in XNB readers, so a game that does not call RegisterAllBuiltInXnbReaders() itself cannot load any .xnb.
tokens: The reader registry is empty by default outside a Game
concepts.note: False at 009d40f5: Game's constructor registers the readers; only tools and tests without a Game must call it. The site states the corrected rule.

concepts.text: Two reader registries share a near-identical name and nothing else: the process-wide ContentTypeReader<T> keyed by canonical name, and the per-manager LooseFileContentTypeReader<T> keyed by type.
The CNJ side is less hardened than the XNB side: the JSON parser has no recursion-depth bound and no size limit, while XNB bounds nesting and sizes and has fuzz harnesses.
SurfaceFormat had 27 values but only Color worked on almost every renderer, and DXT/BC7 were decompressed on the CPU before upload.
tokens: Four separate claims about one format

target.evidence: SurfaceFormat.hpp and Texture validation at 009d40f5; surface-formats page (checked)

concepts.note: At 009d40f5 format support is per renderer and per resource kind; the site separates enumerator, CPU representation, storage and sampling.

concepts.text: CNA has four answers to XNA's .fx: renderer-owned reimplementations, recompiling Microsoft's stock sources with d3dcompiler_47 (61 of 66 shaders matching Microsoft's instruction stream), executing FNA's stock .fxb through MojoShader in FNA3D, and bypassing .fx with ShaderEffect.

target.evidence: modules/renderers/directx9 shaders and FNA3D effect sources at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Corrected: the public Effect(GraphicsDevice&, bytes) constructor is real at 009d40f5, not a throwing stub.

concepts.text: Effect-to-renderer communication goes through the closed GpuDrawParams aggregate; adding a uniform means editing that struct and every renderer.
SpriteBatch destination rectangles were integers, so Vector2 positions were truncated while DrawString rounded.
concepts.note: False at 009d40f5: the shared queue keeps float destinations; whether a fraction survives depends on the renderer seam, as the site explains.

concepts.text: State objects were stored by value on GraphicsDevice, so mutating a state after assignment had no effect and nothing froze a bound state.

target.evidence: BlendState.cpp and siblings (shared_ptr<State> payload with isBound) at 009d40f5

concepts.note: Corrected at 009d40f5: copy construction creates an independent state, copy assignment aliases, and a bound flag exists; the site states the current rules.

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice texture slots (TextureCollection) enforce real invariants but are not a general binding mechanism; textures reach the GPU through effects or ShaderEffect.
tokens: Texture slots are not a general binding mechanism

concepts.text: GraphicsDevice::Reset raises its events and restores presentation state in a defined order rather than recreating the renderer.
concepts.note: The site documents the 009d40f5 reset order and rollback boundary; the pin-era device-loss statement is not carried over.

concepts.text: DrawPrimitivesEx/DrawIndexedPrimitivesEx have default implementations, and a renderer's override presence is not proof that effect parameters are honoured; defaults throw, no-op or degrade depending on the method.
concepts.note: The pin's per-family matrix (including a retired family's silent colored downgrade) is not carried over; the site lists the current default kinds.

concepts.text: Capability answers overclaimed MRT and occlusion queries on several renderers because SupportsCapability defaults to true and the shared test accepted catch-all expectations.
tokens: A capability answer is a hint, not a contract
concepts.note: Per-renderer answers changed after the pin (Known Issues CNA-BUG-054); the site keeps the general rule and the capability matrix.

concepts.text: CNA vertex structures are not blittable: Color and vertex types carry vtable pointers (sizeof(Color) is 24 on 64-bit hosts), so BuiltInVertexStreams defines plain stream structs with static_asserted layouts as the GPU byte truth.
CNA_DEVICES defaults OFF and gates modules/devices-ext, while the faithful Microsoft::Devices::Sensors port in modules/devices is not gated by it.
Compass and Motion are implemented only on Android; elsewhere IsSupported is false because SDL exposes no magnetometer or fused-orientation API.
NetworkSession's Local and LocalWithLeaderboards types deliver no data: RealNetworkingEnabled is true only for SystemLink, although session lifecycle and events are real.

GamerServicesDispatcher::Update() is empty and UpdateAsync returns the initialised flag, so XNA-style 'while (!IsCompleted) UpdateAsync()' loops depend on each Begin*/End* pair completing synchronously.
StorageContainer path resolution had no containment check while only DeleteContainer was guarded.
tokens: DeleteContainer had its own containment check in alpha.1
concepts.note: Fixed after the pin: container names and file/directory paths must stay inside the container (Known Issues CNA-BUG-046); the site states the current rule.

concepts.text: AvatarRenderer's XNA-faithful API is deliberately inert (state is Unavailable), while a separate CNAEXT path (EnableRealRenderingEXT/DrawRealEXT) renders GPU-skinned avatars.

An in-tree glTF 2.0 importer on vendored cgltf is shared by the offline gltf_to_cnj tool and ContentManager, and its conformance apparatus (pinned spec, generated corpus, oracle ladder, executable defect ledger) is the best worked example of method in the tree.
'The importer parses it' and 'the runtime plays it' are separate claims; the pin-era gaps (dropped rigid animation, first mesh group only, unsurfaced warnings) illustrated why.
concepts.note: Several of the pin's example gaps are fixed at 009d40f5 (every group is retained; an import report exists); the rule is kept, the examples are not.

concepts.text: SupportsCapability defaults to true, so a renderer must opt out of 3D and other features; the polarity is a trap.
